idea-plugin.name: Log Injection Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags an unsanitized logging call reachable from an HTTP endpoint parameter -- CWE-117 (Log Injection): an attacker can inject a CRLF sequence to forge fake log entries, hiding a real attack trail or misleading whoever reviews the logs later (SEI CERT IDS03-J, "Do not log unsanitized user input").

Built on a REAL whole-project interprocedural taint analysis -- the base technique real dataflow frameworks use: the actual project call graph, condensed into strongly connected components via Tarjan's algorithm (handling recursion/mutual recursion correctly), with taint summaries computed per method to a real FIXED POINT, not a bounded-depth approximation. The hardest algorithmic technique in this catalog.

Stated honestly: AWS CodeGuru Reviewer has a dedicated log injection detector, but it's CI/batch, not an inline IDE inspection. Qodana's own taint analysis covers OWASP categories A01/A03/A07/A08/A10 -- Log Injection (A09, Security Logging Failures) is NOT among them, and Qodana taint analysis requires a paid Ultimate Plus license regardless (not Community Edition). No dedicated Marketplace plugin found for this exact angle.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

localInspection.displayName: Unsanitized endpoint parameter reaches a logging call
